study_identification_part.si4_title: Cell type-specific manifestations of cortical thickness heterogeneity in schizophrenia

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states research hypotheses and the purpose of applying normative modeling. The study aims to determine whether cortical thickness (CTh) heterogeneity in schizophrenia relates to interregional variation in distinct neural cell types. The purpose is explicitly described: to characterize CTh heterogeneity using normative ranges, explain CTh deviations by cell type gene expression, and stratify patients into cell-based subtypes for understanding biological heterogeneity. Both criteria (research hypotheses/questions and purpose of normative modeling) are met.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Here, we sought to determine whether cortical thickness (CTh) heterogeneity in schizophrenia relates to interregional variation in distinct neural cell types, as inferred from established gene expression data and person-specific genomic variation... To characterize CTh heterogeneity (interindividual variation), normative ranges (i.e., centiles) in regional CTh were defined on healthy controls as a function of age and sex, and CTh deviations were then estimated for each individual with schizophrenia... Biologically valid stratification of patients using cell-based approaches could usher in a new strategy to understand biological heterogeneity in schizophrenia and to address patient variability in planning in vitro disease models.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: All three criteria are satisfied. (1) The meaning and direction of deviation scores are explained: The study describes that deviation scores reflect differences from mean CTh, with infra-normal deviations indicating cortical thinning and supra-normal indicating thicker cortex. Negative correlation values indicate regions where CTh loss maps onto higher cell type gene expression. (2) Quantitative thresholds are reported: Individuals were categorized as within normative range (5th to 95th percentiles) or deviating (outside this range). The 5% and 95% percentiles define the normative range boundaries. (3) Clinical implications are discussed: The study discusses relationships with cell type-specific polygenic risk scores, compares patterns across subtypes (e.g., 'Subtypes I and II were characterized by widespread cortical thinning, in contrast to Subtype III'), notes that 'approximately a fifth had neuronal loading combined with widespread thinning', and discusses limitations including that 'patterns of CTh alterations that do not map neatly onto specific cell types may weaken the predictive power of polygenic risk.'
